questions.question: Which of the following rivers is NOT mentioned in Rigveda?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Krishna**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Rigveda is the oldest of the four Vedas and is a primary source of early Indian history, focusing on hymns, rituals, and nature worship.
 
• Rivers like Saraswati, Sindhu (Indus), and Yamuna are prominently mentioned in the Rigveda as sacred rivers with vital cultural and religious significance.
 
• The Rigveda praises the Sindhu (Indus) as a mighty river, referring to it as the lifeblood of the ancient Vedic civilization.
 
• The Saraswati River, often described as a divine and mythical river, is extensively referenced in the Rigveda, symbolizing fertility and prosperity.
 
• Krishna, a river in southern India, is not mentioned in the Rigveda, as the focus of the text is primarily on rivers in the northwestern and northern regions of the Indian subcontinent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Geographical Context of the Rigveda:** The hymns of the Rigveda were composed in the Sapta Sindhu (land of seven rivers) region, which includes the modern-day areas of Punjab and Haryana.
 
• **Important Rivers in the Rigveda:** The Rigveda mentions rivers like Saraswati, Sindhu (Indus), Ganga, Yamuna, and others, emphasizing their significance in agriculture, rituals, and trade.
 
• **Saraswati River:** The Saraswati River, often considered mythical, is described as flowing between the Yamuna and Sutlej rivers. It is central to Vedic cosmology and is regarded as a sacred river.
 
• **Absence of Southern Rivers:** Rivers like Krishna, Godavari, and Kaveri, located in southern India, are not mentioned in the Rigveda, as the Vedic civilization primarily flourished in northern and northwestern India during its composition.
 
• **Later Textual Developments:** The southern rivers gained prominence in later texts like the Mahabharata, Ramayana, and Puranas, reflecting the geographic expansion of Vedic culture over time.

questions.question: Which was an ancient ocean that existed approximately 250 to 50 million years ago before the evolution of the Indian Ocean?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1,

The correct answer is __**Tethys Sea**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Tethys Sea was an ancient ocean that existed between approximately 250 to 50 million years ago, during the Mesozoic and early Cenozoic eras.
 
• It played a crucial role in separating the supercontinents of Laurasia (in the northern hemisphere) and Gondwana (in the southern hemisphere).
 
• During the Jurassic and Cretaceous periods, the Tethys Sea acted as a biodiversity hotspot, housing a wide range of marine organisms.
 
• As tectonic plates shifted, the Tethys Sea gradually disappeared, giving rise to modern-day seas like the Mediterranean Sea and contributing to the formation of the Indian Ocean.
 
• The remnants of the Tethys Sea are visible today in the form of sedimentary rocks, fossil deposits, and geological features across Europe, Asia, and Africa.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Supercontinents:** Laurasia and Gondwana were two major supercontinents separated by the Tethys Sea during the Mesozoic era.
 
• **Plate Tectonics:** The movement of tectonic plates caused the closure of the Tethys Sea and eventually led to the collision of India with Asia, forming the Himalayas.
 
• **Marine Ecosystems:** The Tethys Sea supported diverse marine ecosystems, including ammonites, corals, and other marine life forms, many of which are now extinct.
 
• **Fossil Records:** Fossil deposits from the Tethys Sea provide valuable insights into the evolutionary history of marine organisms and the Earth's geological past.
 
• **Modern Geological Impact:** The disappearance of the Tethys Sea influenced the formation of various mountain ranges, such as the Alps, Himalayas, and Zagros mountains.

questions.question: Who among the following authored the book ‘Sarvajanik Satyadharma’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jyotiba Phule**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Jyotiba Phule, a prominent social reformer and thinker, authored the book **'Sarvajanik Satyadharma'**.
 
• The book emphasizes equality and justice and was written to challenge the caste system and social injustices prevailing during the 19th century.
 
• Phule used his writings, including 'Sarvajanik Satyadharma,' to advocate for the upliftment of oppressed communities, especially the Dalits and women.
 
• This book reflects his broader philosophy of Satyashodhak Samaj (Society of Truth Seekers), which he founded in 1873 to promote social equality.
 
• Jyotiba Phule’s contributions extended to education reform, where he worked tirelessly to promote the education of women and lower-caste individuals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jyotiba Phule:** Born in 1827 in Maharashtra, he was a pioneer of social reform movements in India and is often referred to as the "Father of Indian Social Revolution."
 
• **Satyashodhak Samaj:** An organization founded by Phule to fight against Brahmanical supremacy and to advocate for the rights of marginalized communities.
 
• **Educational Reforms:** Phule, along with his wife Savitribai Phule, opened the first school for girls in India in 1848, marking a major step towards gender equality in education.
 
• **Other Works:** Jyotiba Phule also authored 'Gulamgiri' (Slavery), which criticized caste-based discrimination and oppression.
 
• **Legacy:** Jyotiba Phule's work laid the foundation for the social justice movements that followed, inspiring leaders like B.R. Ambedkar in their fight for equality and rights for the oppressed.

questions.question: According to the 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, which of the following institutions is responsible for regular and fair elections to the Municipalities?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**State Election Commission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, mandates the establishment of the **State Election Commission** in each state to oversee elections at the municipal level.
 
• The State Election Commission is responsible for conducting **regular, free, and fair elections** to the urban local bodies (Municipalities) and rural local bodies (Panchayats).
 
• Under Article 243K and 243ZA of the Indian Constitution, the powers of superintendence, direction, and control of the preparation of electoral rolls and the conduct of all elections to Panchayati Raj Institutions and Municipalities are vested in the State Election Commission.
 
• The State Election Commission is an independent body, and its composition, tenure, and functions are determined by the respective state governments as per the guidelines of the Constitution.
 
• The Election Commission of India is responsible for conducting elections to the Parliament and State Legislatures, but the **State Election Commission handles local body elections**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **74th Constitutional Amendment Act:**

 
 
• It was enacted in 1992 to provide constitutional status to urban local bodies (Municipalities).
 
• The Act introduced three types of municipalities: Nagar Panchayat, Municipal Council, and Municipal Corporation.
 
• It aimed to strengthen decentralized governance in urban areas.
 
 
 
• **State Election Commissions:**
 
 
• Each state has its own State Election Commission, headed by a State Election Commissioner.
 
• The State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor of the state.
 
• The Commission ensures independent and impartial elections to local bodies.
 
 
 
• **Election Commission of India vs. State Election Commission:**
 
 
• The Election Commission of India (ECI) conducts elections to the Parliament, State Legislative Assemblies, and the offices of the President and Vice President.
 
• The State Election Commission conducts elections to Panchayats and Municipalities.
 
• Both bodies operate independently of each other.
 
 
 
• **Articles 243K and 243ZA:**
 
 
• These articles provide for the establishment and functioning of the State Election Commissions.
 
• They empower the State Election Commissions to oversee the preparation of electoral rolls and conduct of elections to Panchayats and Municipalities.

questions.question: In which year did Indian dancer, Sonal Mansingh receive the Padma Vibhushan, India's second highest civilian award?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2003**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Sonal Mansingh** is one of the most celebrated Indian classical dancers, excelling in Bharatanatyam and Odissi dance forms.
 
• She was honored with the **Padma Vibhushan**, India's second-highest civilian award, in the year **2003**.
 
• The Padma Vibhushan recognizes "exceptional and distinguished service" in any field, including arts, public affairs, science, and more.
 
• Sonal Mansingh is known for her contributions to the promotion of classical Indian dance and culture globally.
 
• She is also a recipient of the **Padma Bhushan** (1992) and the **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award** (1987).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Padma Awards:**

 
 
• The Padma Awards are conferred in three categories: Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Shri.
 
• They are announced annually on the eve of Republic Day.
 
• Padma Vibhushan is the second-highest award, followed by Padma Bhushan and Padma Shri.
 
 
 
• **Indian Classical Dance Forms:**
 
 
• India has eight recognized classical dance forms: Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Odissi, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam, and Sattriya.
 
• Sonal Mansingh is a renowned practitioner of Bharatanatyam and Odissi.
 
 
 
• **Sonal Mansingh's Contributions:**
 
 
• She has used dance as a medium to address social issues and promote Indian cultural heritage.
 
• Her performances often combine storytelling, music, and movement to depict themes from mythology and contemporary life.
 
 
 
• **Recognition for Indian Artists:**
 
 
• The Padma Awards are a testament to India's commitment to honoring its cultural ambassadors.
 
• By recognizing artists like Sonal Mansingh, the awards inspire younger generations to preserve and promote traditional art forms.

questions.question: Who is the 25th Chief Election Commissioner of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4,

The correct answer is __**Rajiv Kumar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Rajiv Kumar** is the 25th Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) of India, appointed on **15 May 2022**.
 
• He succeeded **Sushil Chandra** as the Chief Election Commissioner.
 
• Rajiv Kumar has been serving in various administrative capacities, including roles in the Ministry of Finance and Department of Personnel and Training.
 
• The Chief Election Commissioner is responsible for overseeing elections for the Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, State Legislatures, and the offices of President and Vice President in India.
 
• Rajiv Kumar played a significant role in implementing electoral reforms and ensuring transparency in the election process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Election Commission of India (ECI)**

 
 
• Established in **1950**, the ECI is an autonomous constitutional authority responsible for conducting free and fair elections in India.
 
• The ECI consists of the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and two Election Commissioners (ECs).
 
• It operates under Article **324** of the Constitution of India.
 
 
 
• **Roles and Powers of the Chief Election Commissioner**
 
 
• Ensures the conduct of free and fair elections at national and state levels.
 
• Issues guidelines for political parties and candidates during elections.
 
• Oversees the implementation of the Model Code of Conduct during elections.
 
• Has quasi-judicial powers to settle disputes related to elections.
 
 
 
• **Electoral Reforms**
 
 
• Introduction of Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail (VVPAT) system for transparency.
 
• Digitization and simplification of voter registration processes.
 
• Reforms aimed at reducing the influence of money and muscle power during elections.
 
 
 
• **Significance of ECI**
 
 
• Plays a vital role in upholding India's democratic values.
 
• Ensures the participation of citizens in the electoral process.
 
• Maintains the integrity of the electoral system.

questions.question: The constant number of water molecules present in one formula of a single unit of salt is known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Water of Crystallisation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Water of crystallisation** refers to the fixed number of water molecules that are chemically bound within the crystalline structure of a compound.
 
• It is essential for maintaining the physical properties and structure of the crystal.
 
• Compounds with water of crystallisation are often called **hydrated salts**.
 
• Examples include **copper sulfate pentahydrate (CuSO₄·5H₂O)** and **gypsum (CaSO₄·2H₂O)**.
 
• On heating, these compounds may lose their water of crystallisation, resulting in anhydrous forms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hydrated Salts:** These are crystalline solids containing water molecules within their structure. The water molecules are known as water of crystallisation.
 
• **Anhydrous Compounds:** When hydrated salts lose their water of crystallisation upon heating, they become anhydrous. For example, heating CuSO₄·5H₂O forms anhydrous CuSO₄.
 
• **Efflorescence:** Some hydrated salts lose water of crystallisation naturally when exposed to air. This phenomenon is called efflorescence. Example: Washing soda (Na₂CO₃·10H₂O).
 
• **Deliquescence:** Certain compounds absorb moisture from the air and dissolve in it to form a solution. These are called deliquescent substances, like calcium chloride (CaCl₂).
 
• **Applications:** Water of crystallisation is significant in chemical analysis, construction materials (e.g., plaster of Paris), and in maintaining the stability of certain compounds.

questions.question: In what reference was ‘Growth’ the goal of all the five-year plans?

options.text: Growth of country’s capacity to produce goods and services
Growth in foreign investment in the country
Growth in the import of goods and services in the country

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Growth of country's capacity to produce goods and services**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The term "growth" in the context of the five-year plans refers to the **country's capacity to produce goods and services**, measured by economic indicators like Gross Domestic Product (GDP).
 
• All five-year plans aimed at ensuring **self-reliance, modernization, and economic development** through industrialization, agricultural growth, and infrastructure development.
 
• The primary goal of the plans was to achieve a sustained increase in production capacity to meet the needs of the growing population and reduce reliance on imports.
 
• Economic growth was seen as the cornerstone for improving living standards, reducing poverty, and achieving balanced regional development.
 
• For example, the Second Five-Year Plan (1956–61) emphasized **rapid industrialization** and the growth of capital goods industries to strengthen the economic base of the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gross Domestic Product (GDP):** GDP is the total monetary value of all finished goods and services produced within a country's borders in a specific time period, serving as a primary indicator of economic growth.
 
• **Planned Economy:** India adopted a planned economic model post-independence, where the government played a central role in setting production targets and resource allocation through five-year plans.
 
• **Self-Reliance:** A key objective was to reduce dependence on foreign aid and imports by developing indigenous industries and enhancing production capacity.
 
• **Balanced Regional Development:** Special focus was placed on reducing regional disparities by encouraging growth in backward and underdeveloped areas.
 
• **Role of the Planning Commission:** The Planning Commission (now replaced by NITI Aayog) was responsible for formulating and overseeing the implementation of five-year plans to achieve economic growth and social welfare objectives.

questions.question: The New Year as per the Assamese calendar coincides with the beginning of the harvest season, which is also known as ______ Bihu.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bohag Bihu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bohag Bihu**, also known as **Rongali Bihu**, marks the Assamese New Year and the beginning of the harvest season.
 
• It is celebrated in the month of **April**, typically on the 14th or 15th, and aligns with the harvest festivals in other parts of India like Tamil Nadu's **Puthandu** and Punjab's **Baisakhi**.
 
• This festival spans **three primary days**: Goru Bihu (for cattle), Manuh Bihu (for humans), and Gosai Bihu (for deities).
 
• Bohag Bihu involves traditional dances like the **Bihu dance**, music, and the preparation of delicacies such as **pithas** (rice cakes) and **larus** (sweet snacks).
 
• The festival is rooted in agrarian traditions, celebrating fertility, prosperity, and the bond between humans and nature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Other Types of Bihu:**

 
 
• **Magh Bihu:** Also known as Bhogali Bihu, it is the post-harvest festival celebrated in January, emphasizing feasts and bonfires.
 
• **Kati Bihu:** Observed in October, it is a simpler festival focused on lighting lamps in paddy fields to pray for a good harvest.
 
 
 
• **Agrarian Connection:** Bihu festivals are directly linked to the agricultural cycle of Assam, reflecting the socio-economic dependence on farming.
 
• **Cultural Significance:** Bohag Bihu is a symbol of Assamese identity and unity, transcending religious and ethnic boundaries in the state.
 
• **Bihu Dance:** Recognized worldwide, it is a vibrant folk dance that showcases the energy and spirit of the Assamese people, performed during the festival.
 
• **Assamese Calendar:** Bohag Bihu marks the start of the Assamese calendar year, aligning with the traditional Hindu solar calendar.

questions.question: Magnesium hydroxide is a common ingredient of antacids and laxatives popularly known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2,

The correct answer is __**Milk of Magnesia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Milk of Magnesia is a suspension of magnesium hydroxide in water and is widely used as an **antacid** to neutralize stomach acid and relieve indigestion or heartburn.
 
• It is also used as a **laxative** to treat occasional constipation by drawing water into the intestines, promoting bowel movement.
 
• Magnesium hydroxide reacts with hydrochloric acid in the stomach to form magnesium chloride and water, thereby reducing acidity.
 
• Milk of Magnesia is available in liquid form and is popular due to its gentle and effective action.
 
• It is commonly prescribed in cases of mild digestive disturbances and is considered safe when used in recommended doses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Magnesium Hydroxide:**

 
 
• A chemical compound with the formula Mg(OH)₂, classified as an inorganic base.
 
• It appears as a white powder or suspension and is sparingly soluble in water.
 
• Commonly used in medicine, agriculture, and as a flame retardant in plastics.
 
 
 
• **Antacid Function:**
 
 
• Milk of Magnesia neutralizes excess stomach acid, providing relief from acid reflux, bloating, and heartburn.
 
• Other common antacid ingredients include calcium carbonate, aluminum hydroxide, and sodium bicarbonate.
 
 
 
• **Laxative Effect:**
 
 
• Magnesium hydroxide works as an osmotic laxative, drawing water into the intestines to soften stool.
 
• Recommended for short-term use to avoid dependency or electrolyte imbalance.
 
 
 
• **Safety and Precautions:**
 
 
• Overuse may lead to diarrhea, electrolyte imbalance, or dehydration.
 
• Not recommended for individuals with kidney disease or those on a low-magnesium diet.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution stipulates that the State shall work to promote the educational and economic interests of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 46**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 46 of the Indian Constitution comes under the Directive Principles of State Policy (Part IV).
 
• It mandates the State to promote the educational and economic interests of Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs), and other weaker sections of society.
 
• The provision emphasizes protecting these communities from social injustice and exploitation.
 
• The directive serves as a guiding principle for the government to formulate policies aimed at reducing inequalities and ensuring social justice.
 
• Though not legally enforceable, the principles under Part IV act as a moral obligation for the State.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP):**

 
 
• These are guidelines for the State to ensure socio-economic justice and aim to create a welfare state.
 
• They are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be enforced by the courts.
 
• Part IV of the Indian Constitution (Articles 36-51) deals with the Directive Principles.
 
 
 
• **Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs):**
 
 
• SCs and STs are historically disadvantaged communities recognized in the Constitution.
 
• The Constitution provides special measures to uplift these groups, including reservations in education, employment, and political representation.
 
 
 
• **Social Justice and Equality:**
 
 
• Social justice refers to fair treatment and equal opportunities for all sections of society.
 
• Article 46 aligns with the broader goals of Articles 14 (Equality before the law) and 15 (Prohibition of discrimination).
 
 
 
• **Educational and Economic Measures:**
 
 
• Government schemes such as Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarships, Eklavya Model Residential Schools, and Stand-Up India aim to empower SCs and STs.
 
• Skill development initiatives and financial inclusion programs are part of these efforts.

questions.question: Aajeevika - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM) was launched by the Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD), Government of India in the year _______________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3,

The correct answer is __**2011**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Aajeevika - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM) was launched by the Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD), Government of India, in **June 2011**.
 
• NRLM aims at reducing poverty by enabling the rural poor to engage in sustainable livelihood opportunities through self-help groups (SHGs).
 
• It was designed as a successor to the Swarnjayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY) with a broader focus on livelihood enhancement.
 
• The mission is funded in partnership between the Government of India and the World Bank.
 
• NRLM operates on the principle of **community-driven development**, empowering women and marginalized groups.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Self-Help Groups (SHGs):**

 
 
• SHGs are the backbone of NRLM and consist of 10-20 members who come together to save and improve their financial status.
 
• They also receive training for capacity building, financial literacy, and entrepreneurial skills.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of NRLM:**
 
 
• Focus on women empowerment, with 70% of SHGs comprising women.
 
• Access to credit, skill-building, and market linkages for livelihood enhancement.
 
• Encouragement of sustainable development practices.
 
 
 
• **World Bank Partnership:**
 
 
• The World Bank supports NRLM through financial aid and technical assistance.
 
• It emphasizes community-based institutions for implementation.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Livelihoods:**
 
 
• NRLM promotes agriculture, animal husbandry, handicrafts, and other sustainable livelihoods.
 
• It aims to ensure that the rural poor achieve significant economic independence.

questions.question: As per Census 2011, which of the following southern states has the lowest literacy rate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to Census 2011, Andhra Pradesh recorded the **lowest literacy rate among southern states** at 67.02%.
 
• Among the southern states, Kerala had the **highest literacy rate** at 93.91%, followed by Tamil Nadu at 80.33%, Karnataka at 75.36%, and Andhra Pradesh at the bottom.
 
• The national average literacy rate as per Census 2011 was **74.04%**, making Andhra Pradesh's literacy rate significantly lower than the average.
 
• Literacy rate is calculated as the percentage of literate individuals aged seven years and above in a given population.
 
• The low literacy rate in Andhra Pradesh can be attributed to various factors, including **regional disparities, socio-economic challenges, and lack of access to educational resources**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Literacy Rate Definition:** Literacy rate is defined as the percentage of people aged 7 years and above who can read and write with understanding in any language.
 
• **Kerala's Literacy Model:** Kerala's high literacy rate is often attributed to effective government policies and a strong emphasis on education and health infrastructure.
 
• **National Literacy Mission:** The Government of India launched the National Literacy Mission in 1988 to eradicate illiteracy among adults aged 15 and above.
 
• **Regional Variations:** Literacy rates in India vary significantly across states due to factors like economic development, cultural practices, and accessibility to education.
 
• **Female Literacy:** Female literacy rates are often lower than male literacy rates, highlighting the need for gender-focused educational initiatives.

questions.question: In the monasteries of which state was the Sattriya dance form developed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3,

The correct answer is __**Assam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Sattriya** is a classical dance form of India that originated in the monasteries of Assam.
 
• The dance was introduced in the 15th century by **Srimanta Sankardev**, a Vaishnavite saint and reformer.
 
• Sattriya was initially performed in **Satras** (Vaishnavite monasteries) as a form of religious expression and storytelling.
 
• The dance combines elements of drama, music, and dance to depict stories from Hindu mythology, particularly the life of Lord Krishna.
 
• In 2000, Sattriya was recognized as one of the **eight classical dance forms of India** by the Sangeet Natak Akademi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Srimanta Sankardev:** He was a 15th-century saint, scholar, and cultural icon of Assam who played a key role in the spread of the Bhakti movement.
 
• **Satras:** These are Vaishnavite monasteries established by Srimanta Sankardev and his followers, serving as centers for religion, art, and culture.
 
• **Costumes:** Sattriya dancers wear traditional Assamese attire, including the **dhoti, chadar, and ghuri** for men and the **mekhela chadar** for women.
 
• **Music:** The dance is accompanied by traditional Assamese musical instruments such as the **Khol (drum), taal (cymbals), and flute**.
 
• **Other classical dance forms:** India has eight recognized classical dances, including Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam, Kuchipudi, and Sattriya.

questions.question: From where does the customer get the ability to buy goods and services?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Income is the primary determinant of an individual's ability to buy goods and services, as it directly affects purchasing power.
 
• Higher income levels enable individuals to access a broader range of goods and services, improving their standard of living.
 
• Disposable income, which is the portion of income left after taxes and essential expenses, plays a crucial role in discretionary spending.
 
• Economic theories, such as the Keynesian consumption function, emphasize the direct relationship between income and consumption.
 
• Income inequality significantly impacts the overall demand for goods and services in an economy, as lower-income groups have limited purchasing power.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Purchasing Power:** Defined as the financial ability to buy goods and services, it depends on income levels and inflation rates.
 
• **Disposable Income:** The amount of money individuals or households have available for spending and saving after taxes and essential expenses.
 
• **Consumption Function:** An economic concept that represents the relationship between disposable income and consumer spending.
 
• **Marginal Propensity to Consume (MPC):** The fraction of additional income that is spent on consumption rather than saved.
 
• **Inflation Impact:** Rising inflation can erode purchasing power, reducing the ability to buy goods and services even with the same income.

questions.question: Bhakti Pradip Kulkarni is a famous _______ player.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3,

The correct answer is __**Chess**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Bhakti Pradip Kulkarni is an **Indian chess player** and a FIDE Woman Grandmaster (WGM).
 
• She won the **Asian Chess Championship (Women)** in 2018 held in Makati City, Philippines.
 
• Bhakti has represented India in multiple **international chess tournaments** and has secured several laurels.
 
• She is known for her strategic gameplay and has been a prominent figure in Indian women's chess.
 
• Bhakti Kulkarni has contributed to promoting chess in India by inspiring young players through her achievements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chess Terminology:**

 
 
• **Checkmate:** A position where the opponent's king is under threat and cannot escape.
 
• **FIDE:** Fédération Internationale des Échecs or International Chess Federation, the governing body for chess.
 
• **Opening:** The initial moves in a chess game aimed at controlling the center and developing pieces.
 
• **Endgame:** The final stage of the game where fewer pieces remain on the board.
 
 
 
• **India's Chess Legacy:**
 
 
• India has produced renowned chess players like Viswanathan Anand, a former World Chess Champion.
 
• Chess is believed to have originated in India as "Chaturanga" during the Gupta Empire.
 
 
 
• **Women in Chess:**
 
 
• Women's chess is gaining prominence globally, with various championships held exclusively for women.
 
• Indian women players like Bhakti Kulkarni and Harika Dronavalli have excelled in international chess tournaments.
 
 
 
• **Chess Benefits:**
 
 
• Improves cognitive skills like problem-solving, strategic thinking, and memory enhancement.
 
• Promotes patience, concentration, and decision-making abilities.
